keyFindings.description:
On a CRLF file the first --write leaves a bare CR inside a line ('Some text. More text
here.
' becomes 'Some text.
More text here.
', exit 0), and ODD_WHITESPACE then refuses that file on every later run. The architect's fix (2026-10-28 15:34Z): --write refuses any file that holds a carriage return, CRLF included, naming the file, with a test.

readText decodes with readFile(path, 'utf8'), which turns invalid UTF-8 into U+FFFD, and writeFile saves it: 'Caf\xe9 words here. More words follow.' is written with exit 0 and the byte e9 becomes ef bf bd, a non-whitespace change. Decode with new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }) and refuse the file on error, with a test.

The refusal tests use inputs relayout leaves alone, so deleting the refusal's 'continue' (semantic-line-breaks.ts:1147) passes all tests while the script prints the refusal, exits 2 and still rewrites the file ('Some words. More words.\n<source\fsrc=x> more words.'). Start each input with a line relayout would change; the CR and UTF-8 tests the same way.
